title: Using dygraphs
text: dygraphs package R interface dygraphs JavaScript charting library. provides rich facilities charting time-series data R, including: Automatically plots xts time series objects (object convertible xts). Highly configurable axis series display (including optional second Y-axis). Rich interactive features including zoom/pan series/point highlighting. Display upper/lower bars (e.g. prediction intervals) around series. Various graph overlays including shaded regions, event lines, point annotations. Use R console just like conventional R plots (via RStudio Viewer). Seamless embedding within Quarto/R Markdown documents Shiny web applications. can use dygraphs R console, within R Markdown documents, within Shiny applications. demos dygraphs well quite others articles section website. ’s simple dygraph() created multiple time series object: Note graph fully interactive: mouse moves series individual values displayed. can also select regions graph zoom (double-click zooms ). can customize dygraphs piping additional commands onto original dygraph() object. pipe dyRangeSelector() onto original graph: Note example uses |> (“pipe”) operator compose dygraph() range selector. use similar syntax customize axes, series, options. example: Many options customizing series axis display available. ’s even possible combine multiple lower/value/upper style series single display shaded bars. ’s example illustrates shaded bars, specifying plot title, suppressing drawing grid x axis, use custom palette series colors:
code: library(dygraphs) lungDeaths <- cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths) dygraph(lungDeaths) dygraph(lungDeaths) |> dyRangeSelector() dygraph(lungDeaths) |>   dySeries("mdeaths", label = "Male") |>   dySeries("fdeaths", label = "Female") |>   dyOptions(stackedGraph = TRUE) |>   dyRangeSelector(height = 20) hw <- HoltWinters(ldeaths) predicted <- predict(hw, n.ahead = 72, prediction.interval = TRUE)  dygraph(predicted, main = "Predicted Lung Deaths (UK)") |>   dyAxis("x", drawGrid = FALSE) |>   dySeries(c("lwr", "fit", "upr"), label = "Deaths") |>   dyOptions(colors = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(3, "Set1"))

title: Annotation & Shading
text: can add annotations individual points within plot. minimize visual footprint annotations typically short abbreviations (e.g. “”, “B”, “C”) elaborated upon tooltip adjacent explanatory text. example, following graph annotate dates saw first deployment US combat troops Korea Vietnam: ’s important aspect example note: actual dates two events used annotation. Rather, dates align quarterly boundaries time series used (dygraphs include annotations exactly match one ’s x-axis values). Note want print larger annotation attach x-axis rather individual points can use attachAtBottom width parameters follows: example also demonstrates another concept: writing helper function define common graph element options single place. presAnnotation() function takes dygraph() modifies include annotation requisite layout behavior.
code: dygraph(presidents, main = "Quarterly Presidential Approval Ratings") |>   dyAxis("y", valueRange = c(0, 100)) |>   dyAnnotation("1950-7-1", text = "A", tooltip = "Korea") |>   dyAnnotation("1965-1-1", text = "B", tooltip = "Vietnam") presAnnotation <- function(dygraph, x, text) {   dygraph |>     dyAnnotation(x, text, attachAtBottom = TRUE, width = 60) }  dygraph(presidents, main = "Quarterly Presidential Approval Ratings") |>   dyAxis("y", valueRange = c(0, 100)) |>   presAnnotation("1950-7-1", text = "Korea") |>   presAnnotation("1965-1-1", text = "Vietnam")

title: Annotation & Shading
text: can add shading effect graph background one time ranges. useful highlighting periods time special properties (e.g. holding periods securities). example, following code adds shading effect 1920’s 1940’s New Haven Temperatures graph: Note parameters must type POSIXct (objects directly convertible POSIXct). may want modify color shading make less subtle. ’s version previous graph custom colors shading: Note also changed color series black contrast well custom background colors. also possible add horizontal shading chart. example , shading used show one standard deviation range stock return series.
code: dygraph(nhtemp, main = "New Haven Temperatures") |>   dyShading(from = "1920-1-1", to = "1930-1-1") |>   dyShading(from = "1940-1-1", to = "1950-1-1") dygraph(nhtemp, main = "New Haven Temperatures") |>   dySeries(label = "Temp (F)", color = "black") |>   dyShading(from = "1920-1-1", to = "1930-1-1", color = "#FFE6E6") |>   dyShading(from = "1940-1-1", to = "1950-1-1", color = "#CCEBD6") quantmod::getSymbols("MSFT", from = "2014-06-01", auto.assign = TRUE) ## [1] "MSFT" ret <- ROC(MSFT[, 4]) mn <- mean(ret, na.rm = TRUE) std <- sd(ret, na.rm = TRUE) dygraph(ret, main = "Microsoft Share Price") |>   dySeries("MSFT.Close", label = "MSFT") |>   dyShading(from = mn - std, to = mn + std, axis = "y")

title: Axis Options
text: can customize display axes using dyOptions() function (global options) dyAxis() function (per-axis options). ’s example uses : valueRange used set specific range y axis. axisLineWidth option specifies slightly wider pixel width axis lines. fillGraph option specifies y values filled vertically drawGrid option turns grid axes (’ll demonstrate per-axis basis ). ’s another example customizes axes properties: use number options customize axis display: drawGrid option turns grid x axis includeZero option ensures y axis scaled zero rather low-end ’s range values. axisLineColor gridLineColor options change colors axis grid lines respectively. many options available affect axis display. See documentation dyAxis dyOptions details.
code: dygraph(nhtemp, main = "New Haven Temperatures") |>   dyAxis("y", label = "Temp (F)", valueRange = c(40, 60)) |>   dyOptions(axisLineWidth = 1.5, fillGraph = TRUE, drawGrid = FALSE) dygraph(AirPassengers, main = "Airline Passengers / Month") |>   dyAxis("x", drawGrid = FALSE) |>   dyAxis("y", label = "Passengers (Thousands)") |>   dyOptions(     includeZero = TRUE,     axisLineColor = "navy",     gridLineColor = "lightblue"   )

title: Axis Options
text: plotting multiple series distinct value types can add second Y-axis show distinct value scale. done setting independentTicks option y2 axis assigning one series y2 axis. example: independentTicks option can used determine axis primary (therefore axis grid lines aligned ). order display secondary axis scale least one two axes must specify independentTicks = TRUE. Possible combinations include: y = TRUE, y2 = FALSE: (default) y primary axis y2 ticks aligned ones y. (1 grid) y = FALSE, y2 = TRUE: y2 primary axis y ticks aligned ones y2. (1 grid) y = TRUE, y2 = TRUE: axis independent ticks. (2 grids) example specify y2 axis independent ticks (resulting natural value scale axis labels). also add label Y axis.
code: # define mts with distinct y-axis scales temperature <- ts(   frequency = 12, start = c(1980, 1),   data = c(     7.0, 6.9, 9.5, 14.5, 18.2, 21.5,     25.2, 26.5, 23.3, 18.3, 13.9, 9.6   ) ) rainfall <- ts(   frequency = 12, start = c(1980, 1),   data = c(     49.9, 71.5, 106.4, 129.2, 144.0, 176.0,     135.6, 148.5, 216.4, 194.1, 95.6, 54.4   ) ) weather <- cbind(rainfall, temperature)  # assign the "rainfall" series to the y2 axis dygraph(weather) |>   dySeries("rainfall", axis = "y2") dygraph(weather) |>   dyAxis("y", label = "Temperature (C)") |>   dyAxis("y2", label = "Rainfall", independentTicks = TRUE) |>   dySeries("rainfall", axis = "y2")

title: Plotters
text: plotter draws bar plot rather line plot. ’s ’d create R function wrap Bar Chart plotter: plotter can now used directly within dygraph() pipeline along dygraphs functions:
code: dyBarChart <- function(dygraph) {   dyPlotter(     dygraph = dygraph,     name = "BarChart",     path = system.file("plotters/barchart.js",       package = "dygraphs"     )   ) } dygraph(ldeaths) |>   dyRangeSelector() |>   dyBarChart()

title: Plotters
text: plotter draws multiple column bar chart. ’s ’d create R function wrap Bar Chart plotter: plotter can now used directly within dygraph() pipeline along dygraphs functions:
code: dyMultiColumn <- function(dygraph) {   dyPlotter(     dygraph = dygraph,     name = "MultiColumn",     path = system.file("plotters/multicolumn.js",       package = "dygraphs"     )   ) } lungDeaths <- cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths) dygraph(lungDeaths) |>   dyRangeSelector() |>   dyMultiColumn()

title: Plotters
text: plotters act underlying data dygraph, can also use variations plotters act single series. Several variations come dygraphs package.
code: lungDeaths <- cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths) dygraph(lungDeaths) |>   dyRangeSelector() |>   dyBarSeries("fdeaths") |>   dyFilledLine("mdeaths")

title: Plotters
text: dygraphs comes packaged number group-based plotters. Similar working just single series, can also use custom plotters group data series underlying data. Check documentation Plotters inspiration.
code: lungDeaths <- cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths, ldeaths) dygraph(lungDeaths) |>   dyStackedBarGroup(c("ldeaths", "mdeaths")) dygraph(lungDeaths) |>   dyMultiColumnGroup(c("mdeaths", "fdeaths")) lungDeaths <- cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths, ldeaths, adjustment = 100) dygraph(lungDeaths) |>   dyStackedRibbonGroup(c("fdeaths", "ldeaths")) |>   dyStackedBarGroup(c("adjustment", "mdeaths"))

title: Plotters
text: Use plotters highlight different series, stack related groups, whatever!
code: lungDeaths <- cbind(ldeaths, fdeaths, mdeaths,   additive = rep.int(200, length(ldeaths)),   line = rep.int(3000, length(ldeaths)) ) dygraph(lungDeaths) |>   dySeries("line", strokePattern = "dashed") |>   dySeries("ldeaths", stepPlot = TRUE) |>   dyStackedBarGroup(c("additive", "mdeaths")) |>   dyStackedRibbonGroup(c("fdeaths", "ldeaths"))

title: Labels & Legends
text: several options available customizing appearance behavior plot legend. default legend always appears multiple series appears mouseover single series. default legend shows point values mouse graph mouse leaves. override defaults ensuring legend always visible point values still displayed even mouse leaves plot: enable “follow” mode show legend overlaid plot (near mouse) mouse point: several data series sometime legend mouse-wraps second line. avoid can set legend width something wider default 250 pixels. example:
code: dygraph(nhtemp, main = "New Haven Temperatures") |>   dySeries("V1", label = "Temperature (F)") |>   dyLegend(show = "always", hideOnMouseOut = FALSE) dygraph(nhtemp, main = "New Haven Temperatures") |>   dySeries("V1", label = "Temperature (F)") |>   dyLegend(show = "follow") lungDeaths <- cbind(ldeaths, mdeaths, fdeaths) dygraph(lungDeaths, main = "Deaths from Lung Disease (UK)") |>   dyLegend(width = 400)

title: Plugins
text: “Unzoom” dygraphs plugin adds “Reset Zoom” button graph ’s displaying zoomed state (bit discoverable default double-click gesture unzooming). JavaScript source code Unzoom plugin : https://github.com/rstudio/dygraphs/blob/master/inst/plugins/unzoom.js. ’s ’d create R function wrap unzoom plugin: plugin can now used directly within dygraph() pipeline along dygraphs functions: Try zooming dygraph() note “Reset Zoom” button now appears graph zoomed state.
code: dyUnzoom <- function(dygraph) {   dyPlugin(     dygraph = dygraph,     name = "Unzoom",     path = system.file("plugins/unzoom.js", package = "dygraphs")   ) } dygraph(ldeaths) |>   dyRangeSelector() |>   dyUnzoom()

title: Plugins
text: dyCrosshair plugin draws crosshair line point closest mouse user hovers graph (see JavaScript source code plugin : https://github.com/rstudio/dygraphs/blob/master/inst/plugins/crosshair.js). plugin includes “direction” option provided argument R wrapper function forwarded plugin using “options” argument dyPlugin(). plugin can now used just like dygraphs function can even composed plugins: hover graph ’ll see vertical crosshair drawn current position mouse.
code: dyCrosshair <- function(   dygraph,   direction = c("both", "horizontal", "vertical") ) {   dyPlugin(     dygraph = dygraph,     name = "Crosshair",     path = system.file("plugins/crosshair.js", package = "dygraphs"),     options = list(direction = match.arg(direction))   ) } dygraph(ldeaths) |>   dyRangeSelector() |>   dyUnzoom() |>   dyCrosshair(direction = "vertical")

title: Range Selector
text: can use dyRangeSelector() add range selector bottom dygraph() provides straightforward interface panning zooming. example: can also specify initial date range range selector: Note dateWindow parameter two-element vector POSIXct (objects can unambiguously converted POSIXct). Several options affect appearance range selector:
code: dygraph(nhtemp, main = "New Haven Temperatures") |>   dyRangeSelector() dygraph(nhtemp, main = "New Haven Temperatures") |>   dyRangeSelector(dateWindow = c("1920-01-01", "1960-01-01")) dygraph(nhtemp, main = "New Haven Temperatures") |>   dyRangeSelector(height = 20, strokeColor = "")

title: Series Options
text: can specify alternate color palette series lines using colors option. example, choose palette RColorBrewer:
code: lungDeaths <- cbind(ldeaths, mdeaths, fdeaths) dygraph(lungDeaths, main = "Deaths from Lung Disease (UK)") |>   dyOptions(colors = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(3, "Set2"))

title: Series Options
text: default dygraphs() displays series line, can however plot series step chart follows:
code: lungDeaths <- cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths) dygraph(lungDeaths, main = "Deaths from Lung Disease (UK)") |>   dyOptions(stepPlot = TRUE)

title: Series Options
text: can also fill area underneath series well customize alpha value filling:
code: dygraph(ldeaths, main = "Deaths from Lung Disease (UK)") |>   dyOptions(fillGraph = TRUE, fillAlpha = 0.4)

title: Series Options
text: can include display individual points series well customize size points: Different point shapes available well: possible parameters pointShape : triangle, square, diamond, pentagon, hexagon, circle, star, plus ex.
code: dygraph(ldeaths, main = "Deaths from Lung Disease (UK)") |>   dyOptions(drawPoints = TRUE, pointSize = 2) dygraph(ldeaths, main = "Deaths from Lung Disease (UK)") |>   dyOptions(drawPoints = TRUE, pointSize = 5, pointShape = "triangle")

title: Series Options
text: options can also set per-series basis using dySeries() function. example:
code: dygraph(lungDeaths, main = "Deaths from Lung Disease (UK)") |>   dySeries("mdeaths", drawPoints = TRUE, pointShape = "square", color = "blue") |>   dySeries("fdeaths", stepPlot = TRUE, fillGraph = TRUE, color = "red")

title: Series Options
text: can also customize way series lines drawn. draw wider line custom stroke pattern (dashed line):
code: dygraph(ldeaths, main = "Deaths from Lung Disease (UK)") |>   dySeries("V1", strokeWidth = 2, strokePattern = "dashed")

title: Series Options
text: dyGroup() can replicate options across multiple series pass vector values replicate across series. arguments differ length number series named, argument cycled across named series.
code: lungDeaths <- cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths, ldeaths)  dygraph(lungDeaths, main = "Deaths from Lung Disease (UK)") |>   dySeries("fdeaths", stepPlot = TRUE, color = "red") |>   dyGroup(c("mdeaths", "ldeaths"), drawPoints = TRUE, color = c("blue", "green"))

text: dygraphs package R interface dygraphs JavaScript charting library. provides rich facilities charting time-series data R, including: Automatically plots xts time series objects (object convertible xts). Highly configurable axis series display (including optional second Y-axis). Rich interactive features including zoom/pan series/point highlighting. Display upper/lower bars (e.g. prediction intervals) around series. Various graph overlays including shaded regions, event lines, point annotations. text: Currently dygraphs package provides following plotters: dyBarChart() Draws bar plot rather line plot. provided dygraph features one series, dyBarChart call dyMultiColumn instead. dyStackedBarChart() Draws bar chart stacking underlying series. dyMultiColumn() Draws multiple column bar chart. dyBarSeries() Draws single set bars just provided series. dyStemSeries() Draws single set stems just provided series. dyShadow() extraction _fillplotter dygraph-combined-dev.js,    drawing filled area without line. dyFilledLIne() extraction _fillplotter _lineplotter combo    dygraph-combined-dev.js. dyFilledLine allows users fill single series. dyMultiColumnGroup() multicolumn plotter, subset series, leaving    others plotters. dyCandlestick() Draw candlestick chart. dyCandleStickGroup() Employed provided series,    still plotting others. dyStackerBarGroup() Return data group stacked bars dyStackerRibbonGroup() Return data group stacked ribbons

title: dygraph data series — dySeries
text: dygraph Dygraph add series definition name Name series within data set. name specified series bound implicitly based order within underlying time series object. parameter can also character vector length 3 specifies set input column names use lower, value, upper series shaded bar drawn around . label Label display series (uses name label defined) color Color series. can form "#AABBCC" "rgb(255,100,200)" "yellow", etc. specified global colors option (typically based equally-spaced points around color wheel). axis Y-axis associate series ("y" "y2") stepPlot set, display graph step plot instead line plot. stemPlot set, display graph stem plot instead line plot. fillGraph area underneath graph filled? option compatible error bars. drawPoints Draw small dot point, addition line going point. makes individual data points easier see, can increase visual clutter chart. pointSize size dot draw point pixels. dot always drawn point "isolated", .e. missing point either side . also controls size dots. pointShape shape dot draw. Can one following: "dot" (default), "triangle", "square", "diamond", "pentagon", "hexagon", "circle", "star", "plus" "ex". strokeWidth width lines connecting data points. can used increase contrast graphs. strokePattern predefined stroke pattern type ("dotted", "dashed", "dotdash") custom pattern array even index draw odd space pixels. NULL draws solid line. array even length odd length array expressed smaller even length array. strokeBorderWidth Draw border around graph lines make crossing lines easily distinguishable. Useful graphs many lines. strokeBorderColor Color line border used strokeBorderWidth set. plotter function plots data series. May also set global basis using dyOptions. See dygraphs documentation additional details plotting functions.
